findings.title: Missing destination calendar crashes Google Meet bookings
findings.description:
When `destinationCalendar` is null, undefined, or empty, destructuring leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined. Selecting Google Meet then dereferences `.integration` and throws instead of falling back to Cal Video. `handleNewBooking.ts` explicitly supplies null when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination calendar.

Restore optional chaining on `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` and add coverage for absent and empty destinations.

findings.title: Video references lose their credential IDs
findings.description:
The new mapping sets `credentialId` to undefined for every non-calendar result, discarding the credential returned by `createMeeting()` in `packages/core/videoClient.ts`.

`handleCancelBooking.ts` only deletes the video meeting when its reference contains a credential ID. Consequently, newly created video meetings can remain active after their bookings are cancelled. Preserve `result.credentialId` for video results and test creation followed by cancellation.

findings.title: Non-Google providers route every host to the first destination
findings.description:
`EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents()` now invokes each host’s credential with the complete destination array. Office365 still unconditionally selects the first entry, so another host’s credentials are used against the main host’s calendar ID. This fails when that calendar is inaccessible and targets the wrong calendar when it is shared.

The same first-entry assumption exists in Lark’s creation and attendee creation methods and in `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts`; CalDAV can filter out all calendars and report success without creating an event.

Select the destination matching the current credential, as the Google adapter does, or pass a destination-specific event to each adapter. Cover two-host and mixed-provider bookings.

findings.title: Google update and delete fallbacks cannot select a destination
findings.description:
The fallback runs only when `externalCalendarId` is absent, but searches for a destination whose required string `externalId` equals that absent value. It therefore cannot find a destination. Updates receive an undefined `calendarId`; the analogous deletion logic at lines 315–317 silently targets `"primary"`.

Bookings without a stored external calendar ID previously fell back to the event’s configured destination. Restore a meaningful fallback and test updates and deletion of a secondary-calendar event without `externalCalendarId`.

findings.title: Cancelling a recurring collective booking leaves co-host events behind
findings.description:
Although the outer loop now processes every calendar reference and can fetch another host’s credential, the recurring cancellation branch ignores that resolved credential. It loops only over the booking owner’s credentials and selects only the first calendar reference from each updated booking.

For a collective booking with multiple host calendar events, this repeatedly attempts deletion of the first event while leaving the other hosts’ events active. Match each updated booking’s references to their credentials and delete every matching event. Add a recurring collective cancellation regression test.

findings.title: Organization creation discards the slug when billing is disabled
findings.description:
With `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` false, the changed conditions now store neither `slug` nor `metadata.requestedSlug`, losing the supplied organization URL.

`organizations/createTeams.handler.ts` rejects organizations lacking both fields, and `organizations/publish.handler.ts` requires `requestedSlug` in its billing-disabled path. This breaks subsequent onboarding steps. Preserve the submitted slug according to the billing configuration and cover organization creation and onboarding with billing both enabled and disabled.
